layers.note: A spring ephemeral that flowers in sheets as the snow melts in subalpine meadows and open woods.

moisture.note: Moist ground wet with snowmelt in spring.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; follows the melting snow.

elevation_m.note: Subalpine, about 1,000 to 2,100 m in the Washington Cascades and Olympics.

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to part shade under open conifers.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −8 to 0 °C; gone below −14 °C and above 4 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −28 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −35 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 15 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 18 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 2,600 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 1,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.75, gone by 0.55.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.6.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Avalanche lily grows on Vancouver Island and in southwestern British Columbia, the Olympics and the Cascades of Washington and northern Oregon, in wet maritime mountains (general range knowledge; not checked against PLANTS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
